- Initial live result was 12/24; initial offline result was 8/24. Failures reproduced dropped clauses, unsupported objective surface forms, invented specificity for vague rules, invented questions for objective rules, model paraphrases overriding better source text, subject-first irrelevant-input confirmation gaps, and a fixed guess incorrectly labelled impossible because uniform/structured samples did not contain its six literals.
- Expanded the deterministic compiler with bounded support for arbitrary exact six-number sets, no overlap of even guess values, direct sum-modulo equality, membership plus draw-sum compounds, strict guess ranges, draw-only thresholds, guess-only membership, arbitrary sorted-value counts, generalized distance-plus-exact-position counts, and additional signed sum-difference forms. Source ambiguity is binding (`some`, `better`, `harmonious`, `near-perfect`, etc.), while a deterministic objective source cannot inherit an invented model question. AST-based confirmation for real draw-only/guess-only scope and unspecified endpoints remains unchanged.
- Updated semantic scope consent so both action-first (`ignore the draw`) and subject-first (`the draw does not affect the result`) wording are recognized. Updated rule-test-harness to version 2.2.0: values pinned by guess-membership clauses create directed witnesses, so arbitrary fixed winning guesses are `EXTREME`, not false `IMPOSSIBLE` results.
- Final deterministic result: 24/24 cases and 39/39 fixtures. Final live consolidated result: 24/24 and 39/39 fixtures, using the post-grammar full run plus focused reruns of the ten failures and one final isolated Q2-03 verification. External rules blocked before model use in 4-37 ms; model-backed calls took approximately 53-220 seconds under four-way load, so provider latency/throughput remains an explicit operational weakness.

### 2026-08-11 (Rule compiler H03/G04 semantic fidelity fixed)

- Opened the required documents and context before working: `PRD.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills/tyche-test-and-verify/SKILL.md`, and `docs/rule-proposal-prompt-test-set-3.md`. The implementation follows the test skill's typecheck -> test -> lint -> build verification ladder.
- Fixed H03 as a real compound rule. The deterministic compiler now emits a schema-v3 `and` with two independently executable same-position predicates: every guess/draw pair must be within 6, and at least one pair must be exactly equal. The player-facing interpretation states both clauses. Regression fixtures prove that within-6 with no exact position loses, one exact position with every difference <= 6 wins, and an exact position cannot compensate for another difference of 7.
- Fixed the G04 signed-difference class with one canonical orientation, `guessSum - drawSum`. "At least 10 lower" now compiles to `<= -10`; equivalent digit/word forms are supported. Boundary fixtures prove exactly 10 lower wins, only 9 lower loses, and 10 higher loses. The AST-derived player-facing sentence renders this naturally instead of exposing a confusing negative literal.
- Made the provider compile contract auditable instead of relying on more wording heuristics. Skill version `tyche_rule_compiler_skill_v8` now requires an envelope containing the AST, exact `consumedSpans`, and source-derived `workedExamples`. Production preflight sets `requireProviderEvidence`; missing/partial spans or examples that disagree with runtime execution fail closed with `INTERPRETATION_MISMATCH`. Verified spans and examples are frozen into the artifact, and `sourceSpans` is returned and committed by preflight response version 11.
- Added a deliberate non-regression case for `strictly greater than 10 and strictly less than 90`: one source span may truthfully cover both bounds in the single quantified range condition, so the rejected generic "conjunction implies AST and" heuristic was not reintroduced. A partial span that covers only the lower bound is rejected.
- The changes directly strengthen test-set questions 1, 2, and 6 (correct understanding, correct compilation, and announcement/settlement equivalence). Existing ambiguity, clarification, allowed-input, fixed-outcome, and favouritism/external-dependency suites covering questions 3, 4, 5, 7, and 8 remain green.
- Verified the complete relevant ladders: `@tyche/rule-compiler` typecheck, 62/62 tests, lint with zero warnings, and build; `@tyche/api` typecheck, 141/141 tests, lint with zero warnings, and build; `@tyche/worker` typecheck, 166/166 tests, lint with zero warnings, and build. The API test log's intentional `listener exploded` line belongs to the passing subscriber-isolation test. No live 83-prompt model rerun was needed to establish these deterministic boundary and fail-closed properties.
- Reviewed the final result for inconsistencies: source evidence is mandatory only on the production provider path, deterministic rules retain an explicit full normalized source span, old injected-provider tests remain backward compatible unless they explicitly enable the production evidence gate, persisted-artifact validation accepts schema v3 so H03 survives snapshot restore, no runtime fallback or silent error path was added, and no milestone checkbox was marked because milestone marking requires user confirmation.

### 2026-08-11 (Rule compiler: cardinality misparse and unreachable consistency gate fixed)

- Opened required documents/context before working: `PRD.md` (SS6.4 allowed inputs, SS6.5 DSL/AST representation, SS6.6 vague-rule clarification, SS6.10 rule freezing), `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills`, and `docs/rule-proposal-prompt-test-set-3.md`.
- Fixed F1 root cause A: `adjectiveCountMatch` in `parseMatchCountRule` accepted a generic match action, so the cardinality phrase "its six numbers" — true of every guess and every draw — was read as a match threshold. `"none of its six numbers appear in the official draw"` compiled to `match_count_at_least 6`, the exact logical inverse of the request; `"the sum of its six numbers equals the sum of the six drawn numbers"` compiled to the same thing. The pattern now requires an explicit correctness adjective (`certos`/`corretos`/`acertados`/`correct`/`right`); generic phrasings were already covered by the five other sub-patterns, each of which binds the number to the matching verb far more tightly.
- Widened the zero-overlap branch in `compileSupportedRule`, which was both unreachable behind the misparse and too narrow to match `"none of ITS [six] numbers"`. A qualifier between the determiner and "numbers" (`"none of its EVEN numbers"`) is deliberately still excluded — that is a subset rule, not zero overlap.
- Fixed F2: `validateResolvedAst` now takes an `astSource`. `reviewerAst` was `compileSupportedRule(normalizedText)`, which on the deterministic path is the same call on the same text that produced the AST under review, so it always agreed with itself — silently disabling `REVIEWER_MISMATCH` and, because that gate is guarded by `!reviewerAst`, the interpretation-coverage check written to prevent the turn-55 failure. With `preferDeterministic: true` that was the path most rules take.
- Extended `analyzeInterpretationCoverage` beyond value literals, because a rule can keep every number it stated and still freeze a different rule: added operation coverage over a closed set (`mod`, `parity`, `sum`, `digit`) and membership literals (`"contains the number 13"`). A modulus of 2 counts as parity evidence and a modulus of 10 as digit evidence, and `total_ordered_abs_diff_lte` counts as a sum, so correct compiles are not rejected for naming the same operation a different way.
- Narrowed `UNMODELLED_MATCH_QUALIFIERS` so `"at least one drawn number is above 50"` is no longer read as an overlap count; it is a threshold over filtered numbers. The gap before the comparison verb accommodates the dealer's normalized wording (`"at least one number in the official draw is greater than 50"`) without crossing a clause boundary.
- Added four regression tests in `packages/rule-compiler/src/index.test.ts` covering the cardinality misparse, the now-reachable coverage gate, dropped operations (with correct-compile counter-cases), and the filtered-threshold misread.
- Verified: `typecheck`, `lint --max-warnings=0` and `node --test` green for `@tyche/rule-compiler` (58/58), `@tyche/rule-runtime` (20/20), `@tyche/rule-test-harness` (6/6), `@tyche/api` (141/141), `@tyche/worker` (166/166) and `@tyche/web` (247/247). Full 83-prompt corpus re-run against the live pipeline: accepted rules whose behaviour matches the prompt went 12 -> 18, accepted rules whose behaviour contradicts it went 6 -> 2, and unmeasurable went 11 -> 0. None of the 14 rules that already compiled correctly regressed.
- Two accepted-but-wrong cases remain and are recorded rather than papered over: `H03` (a dropped conjunct with no value literal and no operation cue — a generic conjunction rule was rejected because it false-positives on legitimate single-node range rules) and `G04` (the provider inverts a comparison bound). `G04` is not a regression: it was unmeasurable before, and exposing the AST is what made it visible.
- Reviewed the result for inconsistencies: no fallback was introduced and nothing was made to pass by loosening a gate — every fix either narrows an over-broad pattern or restores a check that was silently disabled, and each newly rejected rule fails closed. Model-driven outcome classes still vary between runs (finding F12), which is why the before/after comparison is stated on the deterministic behaviour metric rather than on outcome labels. Three prompts returned `RULE_AGENT_BAD_RESPONSE` during the re-run and returned normal outcomes on retry with no stack traces in the API log, confirming provider flakiness rather than a fault introduced here. The temporary API instance was stopped afterwards and no milestone checkbox was marked, because milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.

### 2026-08-11 (Compiled AST exposed on the rule preflight response)

- Opened required documents/context before working: `PRD.md` (SS6.5 DSL/AST representation, SS6.10 rule freezing, SS7.5 compilation flow), `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills`, and `docs/rule-proposal-prompt-test-set-3.md`.
- `POST /rule-preflight` now returns the compiled `ast` on `RulePreflightResult`, closing the verification gap recorded in test session 3. The official interpretation is derived from the AST, so prose alone can never expose a rule that compiled into something other than what the player wrote; returning the artifact makes "the announcement is the rule" checkable by executing it through `@tyche/rule-runtime`.
- The field is not gated on `decision`: a rule that compiled and was then rejected (re-proposal gate, scope confirmation, trivially-true) is exactly the case where the AST explains the verdict. `decision` and `compiledArtifactHash` remain the acceptance signals and are unchanged.
- `ast` is included in the hashed `preflightResult` payload and its `version` moved from `9` to `10`, so the commitment continues to cover everything the player is shown rather than only the prose about it.
- Typed as `ast?: RuleAst | null` rather than required, because `RuleProposalRecord` extends `RulePreflightResult` and proposals persisted before this field existed do not carry it; every preflight response sets it. This matches the existing convention for `compiledArtifactHash` on the same interface. The interpret phase (`RuleInterpretationResult`) deliberately still carries no AST.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @tyche/api typecheck`, `lint --max-warnings=0`, and `node --test` (141/141 pass); `pnpm --filter @tyche/web typecheck` (the web client type carries an index signature, so the added field is non-breaking); live round trip against the API on `127.0.0.1:3099` confirming `ast` is present and executable, including a direct reproduction of the session-3 `A03` defect where the prompt says win and the returned AST says lose.

### 2026-08-11 (Rule agent behaviour test session 3)

- Opened required documents/context before working: `PRD.md` (SS6.4, SS6.4.3, SS6.6, SS6.10, SS7.1-7.5), `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills`, `docs/product-rule-summary.md`, `docs/rule-proposal-prompt-test-set.md`, and `docs/rule-proposal-prompt-test-set-2.md`.
- Added `docs/rule-proposal-prompt-test-set-3.md`: 83 new prompts in 8 groups plus the full results of running them against the live `POST /rule-preflight` pipeline (`nemotron-3-super:cloud` primary, `granite4.1-guardian:8b` guardian, escalation model unset). Unlike sets 1 and 2 this session adds a behaviour oracle: every accepted rule's AST is re-derived from the pipeline's `normalizedText` and executed through `@tyche/rule-runtime` against win/lose fixtures written from the prompt, so "what is announced is what happens" is measured rather than read.
- Result: 41 pass, 34 fail, 8 unverified. 29 rules were accepted; of the 18 that could be behaviour-checked, 6 (`A02`, `A03`, `A11`, `D07`, `G02`, `H03`) evaluate to something different from what the prompt asked, all at `finalConfidence: 0.936` with `guardianGrounded: true`.
- Critical findings recorded (no code changed in this session): the cardinality word "six" is parsed as a match threshold by `adjectiveCountMatch` so `"none of its six numbers appear in the draw"` compiles to `match_count_at_least 6`; `analyzeInterpretationCoverage` is unreachable on the deterministic compile path because `reviewerAst` is the same `compileSupportedRule(normalizedText)` call as the AST under review, which leaves the turn-55 regression reachable; compound `X and Y` rules silently lose a clause; group D (outcome-determining rules, which are allowed by product policy) scored 0/7; two vague rules (`B09`, `H05`) were accepted with an invented interpretation and no confirmation, contrary to PRD SS6.6.
- Also recorded: prohibited-input gate word gaps (`wallets` plural, Telegram group, `voted`, NFT ownership, player counts) that route eight favouritism/external prompts to `CLARIFY` instead of `BLOCK`; `E06` compiles offline to a fully valid ranking rule and was rejected by the live API only through a re-proposal signature collision; the re-proposal gate masked five mis-compilations by reporting the wrong rule as "already the Rule of the Hour"; `describeRuleAstForPlayers` emits unreadable prose for nested ASTs (`G07`); one guardian false positive (`B02`); one `RULE_AGENT_BAD_RESPONSE` (`F10`).
- Verified: 83/83 prompts executed against the running API on `127.0.0.1:3099` (74 minutes of model time, median 60 s per prompt); every compiler-level claim additionally reproduced offline through `validateAndPrecompileRule` and `evaluateRule` so it holds without the model in the loop; `@tyche/rule-schema`, `@tyche/rule-runtime`, `@tyche/rule-test-harness` and `@tyche/rule-compiler` rebuilt before the run.
- Reviewed the result for inconsistencies: this session is documentation only - no runtime, compiler, contract, database, or configuration change was made, the temporary API instance was stopped afterwards, and no milestone checkbox was marked because milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.

### 2026-08-10 (Prize-vault solvency: rollover sweep, claim reservation, turn-50 recovery)

- Reopened the required `PRD.md` and `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md`, inspected `.claude/skills`, and followed the local Solana contract-upgrade and test-and-verify guidance. `PRD.md` §8.7 defines rollover as money moving to the next turn's same-category bucket; the implementation had it as accounting only.
- Diagnosed a reported `custom program error: #6068` on a winner claim. `6068` is `InsufficientVaultBalance`. The failing claim is turn `50` (`95,000,000` lamports, wallet `EAoZrh8T...`), not the expired turn-`24` card shown beside the error; turn `24` was already paid on 2026-07-13 by `47nY8K3d...`. Root cause: `prize_vault` is a per-turn PDA that only ever receives its own turn's fee share, while the API computes a winner payout from `currentTurn + rollover`, so any turn won with rollover in its pool records a claim larger than its vault. Vault `50` held `61,750,000` spendable against a `95,000,000` claim, and `0.42125 SOL` sat stranded across the vaults of turns `7, 14, 18, 24, 34, 36, 41, 48, 49`.
- Recovery (broadcast, devnet): transferred the exact `33,250,000`-lamport shortfall from the turn authority into the turn-`50` prize vault (`WpxT3Q8Lymsm...`). Added `apps/worker/src/devnet-fund-prize-vault.ts`, which reads outstanding claims from the chain (not the in-memory API), computes the shortfall against the rent-exempt minimum, and is dry-run by default behind `TYCHE_VAULT_TOPUP_BROADCAST=1`.
- Programme changes: `record_claim` now reserves each payout against the turn's `prize_vault`, rejecting an unpayable amount with the new `ClaimExceedsPrizeVault`; `claim_prize` no longer double-decrements and instead clamps the unreserved counter to what the account can back, which self-heals vaults written before the reservation existed. New authority-gated `sweep_prize_rollover` moves a closed turn's whole unreserved balance into the open turn's vault and accumulates the declared split into the destination `TurnState`, guarded by `RolloverAmountMismatch` (declared halves must equal the source balance, making it self-reconciling and replay-safe), `InvalidRolloverDirection`, and `PrizeVaultHasOutstandingClaims` (a vault whose free lamports exceed its unreserved counter still owes a winner and cannot be swept). All four new error codes are appended so existing codes are unchanged.
- Worker changes: `record_claim` now passes the prize vault; `sweepPreviousTurnRollover` runs immediately after a turn opens in both the automation loop and manual turn control, deriving the total from the chain and using the API's rollover record only to split it between buckets; an unsweepable source is skipped off-chain so an unclaimed payout cannot wedge the loop.

### 2026-08-08 (Rule preflight reattach: reopening a conversation picks the run back up)

- Opened the required `PRD.md` (§6.15.1 _Resumable preflight jobs_), `TASK-TEMPORARIA.md`, and `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md`; inspected `.claude/skills` and followed `tyche-test-and-verify` for the verification order. No milestone checkbox or status was changed; milestone marking still requires explicit user confirmation.
- Reported defect, reproduced from live evidence: a rule sent at `2026-08-07T23:36:44Z` ran the full chain and produced a successful interpretation at `23:45:29Z` (Ollama `server.log` plus the operational-state snapshot write in the same second), yet the draft `client:42:21862e73…` was never updated past `23:36:44Z` and the player saw no reply. The result was produced and dropped because no client ever reattached to the job.
- Root cause: every entry point into the Create screen disabled the reattach. Both mount effects bailed on `activeDraftId || chatId || seed || newConversationKey > 0`, and `newConversationKey` only counts up — so the first "Create a rule" click killed reattachment for the rest of the page session. The remaining entry point, "Resume" from the conversation list, sets `chatId` _and_ `seed` and rehydrated the transcript without ever consulting a job pointer. The one route that still worked, a direct load of `/play/propose`, is exactly what the existing e2e suite drove, which is why the gap stayed green.
- Second root cause: the durable half of the pointer never existed. The API validated and stored `preflightJobId` on a conversation draft, but the web only ever sent `null`, and `saveConversationDraft` dropped the field on any save that omitted it — contradicting the contract documented in `conversationDraft.ts`. Every draft in the database had the field empty. The `2026-08-07` entry below states the pointer is persisted "on the conversation draft"; that was never true and is corrected here.
- Web: replaced the leaked `newConversationKey` guard with an explicit `createIntent` (`new` / `resume` / `seed` / `null`) derived per navigation by `resolveCreateIntent`, and folded the three mount effects into one ordered reattach — in-memory run, then draft record, then `localStorage` pointer. A resume now opens with the draft's full transcript instead of collapsing the chat to a single bubble, a replay cursor is never carried across to a different job id, and a pointer past its window clears both copies and shows the existing expired card.
- Web: the run writes `preflightJobId` to the draft as soon as the job is accepted, so the pointer survives a reload in any browser; the conversation list shows a `● compiling` badge and a `Reconnect` action while the pointer is inside the window the API can still answer for.
- Shared `PREFLIGHT_JOB_RUNNING_TTL_MS` through `@tyche/constants` and widened the client's staleness check to the API's real worst case (up to 15 min running, then 10 min retained). Counting only the terminal TTL from `startedAt` left roughly 75 s of usable resume window on the ~9-minute run that failed.
- Coverage added: draft-pointer merge semantics in the API (omit preserves, explicit `null` clears, cleared stays cleared); the durable pointer being written while the job is still running and cleared on the way out; a resume rendering the transcript it was handed; and a new `conversationResume.test.ts` covering navigation-intent derivation, pointer precedence, cursor isolation, and transcript reconstruction.
- Verification passed: `@tyche/constants` `4/4` tests and ESLint zero warnings; `@tyche/api` typecheck, `137/137` tests, ESLint zero warnings; `@tyche/web` typecheck, `221/221` tests, ESLint zero warnings, and production build; `@tyche/worker` typecheck; `git diff --check` clean. Playwright `rule-run-resume`, `rule-proposal`, and `rule-clarification-loop` ran `11/11` green twice consecutively (two earlier single-test failures were dev-server recompile flakes: each was a different spec and neither reproduced across three isolated repeats).
- Live verification against the running API confirmed the merge fix end to end: a draft saved with a job id keeps it across a save that omits the field, an explicit `null` clears it, and a later omitting save does not resurrect it. Not covered end to end: reopening from the conversation list in Playwright, which needs a wallet-connected harness the e2e suite does not have (`NEXT_PUBLIC_UI_MOCK` is a separate dev server and Next 16 allows only one per project dir). That path is covered by unit tests, not by a browser run.
- Environment note, unrelated to this change: **two API processes are bound to port 3002** — the host `tsx watch` (parent PID 26120) and the `tyche-api` container. Requests land nondeterministically on one of them, which makes any live debugging unreliable. The container also ships its own `packages/constants` build and does not see host edits (Docker on Windows does not propagate inotify to bind mounts). One synthetic draft (`live-merge-check`, wallet `4bYqf3rJ…`, not the owner's) remains in the host process's memory from the live check; it is absent from the database and will disappear on the next restart of that process.

### 2026-08-07 (Resumable rule preflight jobs)

- Opened the required `PRD.md` and `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md` and inspected `.claude/skills` before starting. No milestone checkbox was changed; milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.
- Fixed the reported defect: the rule preflight pipeline was bound to the lifetime of its HTTP response, so a dropped socket discarded a completed run (`writeRulePreflightStreamEvent` simply stopped writing while the pipeline ran to completion). A preflight run is now a job owned by a registry, and every transport is a view onto it — detaching a reader never cancels the pipeline.
- Extracted the whole HTTP router into an exported `handleApiRequest`, which was previously unreachable from tests inside `isMainModule()`. Pure move, no logic change; it enables the package's first real HTTP test.
- Added the job registry (opaque 192-bit CSPRNG ids, bounded ring buffer, per-event size cap, running/total/reader caps, lazy TTL sweep with no module timer), folded only terminal jobs into the existing `api_state_snapshots` blob, and shared `PREFLIGHT_JOB_TTL_MS` through `@tyche/constants` so the client cannot drift from the server.
- Added `POST /rule-preflight` with `accept: text/event-stream` returning `202 { jobId }`, and `GET /rule-preflight/jobs/:id/events` serving SSE with per-event ids, `Last-Event-ID`/`?cursor=` replay, a `reset` frame for a cursor outside the buffer, 15s heartbeats, backpressure disconnection, and `404` for an expired job. The legacy NDJSON transport and the blocking JSON transport (used by the devnet seeder) are rewired onto the same registry and are unchanged on the wire.
- Deliberate behaviour change: preflight no longer withholds a good result when the state snapshot write fails. It is a read-only advisory computation that mutates no game state, authorizes no payment and gates nothing on-chain, so `api_state_persistence_failed` no longer appears in its stream; the persist-before-ack rule stays in force for the paid mutating routes.
- Web: replaced the two NDJSON POST helpers (and their duplicated inline reader) with `startRulePreflightJob` + `consumeRulePreflightJob` over a new `sseStream.ts` reader — `fetch` rather than `EventSource`, because `EventSource` cannot resume after a reload, cannot distinguish an expired job from a flaky network, and never gives up reconnecting. Expiry and give-up are dedicated error types that deliberately do **not** extend `ApiRequestError`, so an expired run can never be classified as a rule the compiler refused.
- Web: `conversationRun` now splits into start/resume/settle, the run snapshot carries the job and a separate `connection` field, and the job pointer is persisted in `localStorage` and on the conversation draft so a reload, a killed tab, or reopening the conversation reattaches. `Create.tsx` gained a yellow reconnecting spinner, a `● reconnecting` header state, and a "Connection lost → Reconnect" / "This run expired → Run again" card; red stays reserved for hard failures.
- Web: the Next proxy now forwards `last-event-id`, exempts SSE from the 300s whole-request deadline (which would otherwise recreate the original bug), follows the client's abort signal instead of leaking the upstream socket, and marks SSE responses unbufferable; the service worker steps aside for event streams.
- Found and fixed a real defect while testing the reader: the reconnect budget reset on every accepted connection, so a server that accepts and immediately closes would have looped forever. The budget is now refunded only when the cursor actually advances.
- Verification passed: `@tyche/api` typecheck, ESLint zero warnings, `129/129` tests (including a new HTTP test that drops the socket mid-run and proves the resumed cursor still delivers the result); `@tyche/web` typecheck, ESLint zero warnings, `206/206` tests; `@tyche/worker` typecheck after the shared-constant change; `11/11` Playwright rule-authoring scenarios including a new resume suite covering mid-stream drop, page reload, and expired job. The 13 Playwright specs that stub no network (`number-picker`, `wallet-flow`, `share-card`, `public-round`, `turn-cycle`, and similar) fail in this environment for an unrelated reason: the worker reports `hasActiveTurn: false`, so there is no open turn to render. They touch none of the changed modules.
- Final consistency review: no on-chain state, database record, automation configuration, or milestone checkbox was modified. `POST /rule-preflight` remains unauthenticated, and the new active-job cap is what replaces the accidental rate limiting the old ~150s socket hold provided — a per-principal limit is still absent and is recorded as follow-up, not as fixed.

### 2026-07-09 (Live rule precompilation loop — fixes always-`original_only` election)

- Opened required documents/context before working: `PRD.md` (§6.6/§6.12/§7.9 background precompilation and original-only path), `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md`, `.claude/skills`, and `.claude/skills/tyche-test-and-verify/SKILL.md`.
- Diagnosed a real gap in the live flow: a rule submitted through the app lands on-chain as `RuleProposal { state: Proposed, precompilation: Pending }`, but nothing in the running app moved it to `Eligible`. The AI validation (`runRuleValidationCycle` / API `/rule-validations/run`) and the on-chain `precompile_rule` instruction were only ever exercised by the devnet seed operators (`devnet-seed-real-inputs.ts`, `devnet-10-player-simulation.ts`); the web app only displays precompile status and the worker's two loops (turn-automation, settlement) never validate/precompile. Result: every turn with real user rules had an empty eligible pool and the election correctly fell to `original_only` (observed live on turn 105 with 1 submitted rule + 1 vote).
- Added `apps/worker/src/precompile-loop.ts`: an env-gated (`TYCHE_RULE_PRECOMPILE_ENABLED`, OFF by default), authority-signed loop that runs during phase 1 (before the on-chain `rule_election_cutoff_bps`). Each pass fetches the active turn's still-`proposed`/`pending` rules from the API, runs the deterministic compiler via `/rule-validations/run` (stores the artifact + projects `eligible`), and records the real on-chain `precompile_rule` with the API-returned artifact hash so on-chain state, the frozen election hash, and the stored artifact reconcile. Idempotent (skips rules already moved out of proposed/pending), re-checks the cutoff before every send, and never precompiles an `INVALID` rule. No mocks, no fallbacks; reuses the tested `createPrecompileRuleInstruction`.
- Wired the loop into the worker entrypoint (`apps/worker/src/index.ts`) alongside the settlement loop, and enabled it in `.env` for local/devnet dev.
- Added `apps/worker/src/precompile-loop.test.ts` (7 cases): precompiles a valid proposed rule, validates-but-never-sends for invalid, idempotent skip of already-eligible/invalidated, cutoff-passed guard, mid-pass cutoff break, no-active-turn, and disabled-flag.
- Verified locally: `pnpm --filter @tyche/worker typecheck`, `test` (95/95), `lint` (0 warnings), `build`.
- Verified live on devnet (turn 106): proposed one real rule on-chain in `Proposed`/`Pending` WITHOUT precompiling it, then the running loop precompiled it — `precompile turn=106 rule=1783638979079769 signature=BmCEyt8J…`; API projection moved to `state: eligible` / `precompilationStatus: passed`; and the on-chain election candidate now reads `isEligibleState: true` / `isPrecompiledValid: true` (source of truth), so it will enter the shortlist/election instead of `original_only`.
- Separately observed (not fixed here): the full LLM rule-preflight harness (`/rule-preflight`) can exceed Node's undici 300s headers timeout when the local Ollama model is cold/slow; the precompile loop itself uses the fast deterministic compiler and is unaffected. No milestone checkbox/status was changed — milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.

### 2026-07-06 (Shortlist decision window + claim visibility; conversation history overflow)

- Opened required documents/context before working: `PRD.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills/tyche-ui-coherence/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/playwright/SKILL.md`, and the active plan `groovy-sleeping-comet.md`.
- Diagnosed the manual-test report that a turn ends without ever showing the shortlist/elimination phase or the claim period. Root causes: (1) no code path ever populated the API `RuleEliminationRecord` — `saveRuleElimination` was only called from tests, so `decisionWindowClosesAt/OpenedAt` were always `null` and the web `decisionEndsAt`/countdown never rendered; (2) `useRound` fetched the round summary once (no polling), so post-window phases could never surface live; (3) `decisionPhase` was computed in context but unused by any screen, and Home had no claim surface.
- Worker: `settlement-scheduler.ts` now projects the elimination decision window to the API — publishes an `open` record (with the real on-chain `elimination_window_start/end` timestamps) when the finalist VRF settles, and a `closed` record (with `closedAt`, eliminated/survivor rule ids and hashes) after `close_elimination_window`. Added `ApiBridge.publishRuleElimination` and the `PublishedRuleElimination` shape.
- API: added `POST /rule-eliminations` with `isValidRuleEliminationProjection` validation and `projectRuleElimination`, which merges the worker's on-chain window/outcome with the API's per-finalist vote tallies and saves via `saveRuleElimination`.
- Web: `useRound` and `usePlayerClaims` now poll every 10s (plus window focus), matching `useActiveTurn`; Home shows a yellow "Shortlist decision window" banner (countdown + link to the finalists tab) while `elimination.status === "open"` and a green "Prize ready to claim" banner when the wallet has `availableLamports > 0`; the Rules screen auto-switches to the Finalists tab when the decision window opens.
- Conversation history overflow: `ConversationRow` in `Profile.tsx` now clamps `lastMessage` to two lines (`-webkit-box` line clamp), fixing cards growing unbounded after full transcripts began persisting.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint --max-warnings=0`, and `node --test` all green for `apps/api` (61/61), `apps/worker` (86/86), `apps/web` (8/8); live round-trip smoke test of `POST /rule-eliminations` → `GET /api/v1/turns/{id}/elimination` against the running dev API; browser render check of Home at 390px (`output/playwright/home-390.png`) with no console errors. The temporary web dev server was stopped afterward.

### 2026-07-01 (Rule composer incremental refinements)

- Opened required documents/context before editing: `PRD.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills/develop-frontend/SKILL.md`, and `.claude/skills/tyche-test-and-verify/SKILL.md`.

- Problem: the automatic turn worker was stopped, so no turn was open on devnet and the live round rendered empty (the web reads the active turn directly from devnet RPC via `fetchActiveTurnSnapshot`; the existing web mock only fakes HTTP API endpoints, not the on-chain turn). - Implemented `apps/worker/src/manual-control.ts` reusing the same on-chain instructions as the automatic loop (so the UI keeps reading real devnet state): `openTurnManually` (open next turn, then reset the duration cycle to a comfortable playable window), `closeTurnManually` (shrink the active turn's duration slot to 1s via `set_turn_duration_cycle` so `end_timestamp` moves into the past, then `close_turn`; the on-chain `close_turn` enforces `clock >= end_timestamp`, so early close is impossible without this), and `cycleTurnManually` (close + open). Legacy-account close falls back to `force_skip_legacy_active_turn`, mirroring the automatic loop.
- Exported the shared helpers needed for reuse from `turn-automation.ts` (`fetchGlobalConfig`, `fetchTurnState`, `createOpenTurnInstruction`, `createCloseTurnInstruction`, `createSetTurnDurationCycleInstruction`, `createForceSkipLegacyActiveTurnInstruction`, `deriveAuthorityAddress`, `SolanaAddress`).

Gated behind `TYCHE_TURN_MANUAL_CONTROL_ENABLED` (paths return 404 when disabled, so they stay invisible in production); `/health` now reports `manualControl: "disabled" | "enabled" | "error"`.
- Added env wiring in `docker-compose.yml` (worker): `TYCHE_TURN_MANUAL_CONTROL_ENABLED` (default `false`) and `TYCHE_TURN_MANUAL_OPEN_DURATION_SECONDS` (default `3600`), with a comment marking them test-only. Production keeps the automatic timed loop.

### 2026-06-21 (M4.3/M4.4 divergence closure + M4.5 rollover implementation)

- Opened required project context before working: `PRD.md` (§2.5/§2.6 prize pool, §5.4 lifecycle, §15.5 M4.1–M4.6) and `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md`, and reviewed `.claude/skills` for a relevant skill (no rollover-specific skill; followed best-practices conventions).

Verified both are implemented in `apps/api/src/index.ts` (`calculateRewardDistribution`, `CreatorRewardRecord`/`VoterRewardRecord`, `ClaimRecord`, `/reward-records*`, `/claim-records*`) and green (`pnpm --filter @tyche/api test`, 26/26 before this work). Added tracker rows for M4.3 and M4.4 (Completed, Confirmed 2026-06-21) and explicit rows for M4.5 (In Review) and M4.6 (Not started) so the table now mirrors the PRD.
- **Implemented M4.5 — Rollover Behavior** in the API (`apps/api/src/index.ts`):
  - `settleTurnRollover(turnId)` settles a finished turn's buckets into the next turn via the existing `saveTurnRollover`/`TurnRolloverRecord`: a no-winner bucket rolls its full total forward (so repeated no-winner turns accumulate, since the inbound rollover is part of the next turn's bucket total), and a winner bucket rolls only its integer-division dust, so no lamport is ever lost.
  - `getTurnRolloverSettlement(turnId)` and `getRolloverActivityEvents(turnId)` expose the settlement and a PRD §4.7 Loop-5 "no winner, pool rolls over" spectator-feed event (dust-only remainders are silent).
  - Round summary now carries `activity` + `rolloverSettlement`; new endpoints `POST /turn-rollovers/settle` and `GET /turn-rollovers/settlement` (added to CORS allowlist); reset clears the new settlement map.
  - Rewards are explicitly unaffected (creator/voter rewards draw from a separate platform-monetization reserve, not the prize buckets).
- **Web**: completed the `RoundPage` `RoundSummary` type with `pool.accounting` rollover fields plus `activity`/`rolloverSettlement`, and added a "Rollover" block to the prize-pool tab showing inbound rollover per bucket and the no-winner rollover event(s) / settlement outcome, with matching `globals.css` styles.
- **Tests** (`apps/api/src/index.test.ts`): added "rollover settlement carries no-winner buckets forward and accumulates across repeated no-winner turns" and "rollover settlement pays accumulated pool to a winner after rollover without rolling that bucket again" (also asserts reward accounting is undisturbed and settlement is idempotent).
- Verification passed: `pnpm --filter @tyche/api test` (28/28), `pnpm --filter @tyche/api typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @tyche/api lint`, `pnpm --filter @tyche/web typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @tyche/web lint`, and `pnpm --filter @tyche/web test:e2e -- public-round.spec.ts` (3/3).

### 2026-06-15 (Re-proposal gate: no repeating a rule that held a mandate)

- User-chosen policy: a rule that was **elected as the active Rule of the Hour** in a past turn cannot be proposed again **verbatim**; it may only return if the new proposal adds a **differentiating condition** (a clause in the DSL).
- Identity is the rule's MEANING, not its text: new helpers in `apps/api/src/index.ts` — `ruleSignature(ast)` hashes a **canonicalized** AST and `getMandatedRuleSignatures()` collects the signatures of every settled election's active rule (via `getRuleValidation(turnId, activeRuleId).compiledArtifact.ast`). Canonicalization flattens `and`/`or`, drops single-clause wrappers (`and[X]`≡`X`), collapses double negation, and sorts commutative operands (`and`/`or` clauses, `intersection`, `arith add/mul`) — so the gate **cannot be bypassed cosmetically**; only a substantive added clause changes the signature.
- `createRulePreflight` now blocks when the compiled rule's signature is already mandated (`reproposalBlocked`), setting `needsClarification` + a message telling the player to add a condition. New `RulePreflightResult` field `reproposalBlocked`; folded into `preflightResultHash` (v5).
- Tests: 17/17 `@tyche/api` — `ruleSignature` canonicalization (trivial wrappers/commutative collapse to the same signature; an added clause differs) and `getMandatedRuleSignatures` collection from a settled election. Typecheck clean.
- Notes/limits: the mandated set is computed per preflight from in-memory elections+validations (fine at this scale; would be a query at DB scale). A mandated rule whose validation AST isn't stored cannot be signed/blocked (graceful).
- **PRD updated**: §6.13 rewritten as "Rule Scope and Mandate-Based Re-Proposal Gate" (replaces the time-based cooldown with the canonical-AST-signature mandate gate); §6.15 rewritten as "Rule Preflight and Canonical-Signature Re-Proposal Gate" (replaces semantic-embeddings dedup / `preflight_token` / `RuleDedupResult` with the deterministic implemented preflight + signature gate). The §6.13 cooldown and §6.15 semantic dedup are no longer the spec — superseded by what is implemented.
- **Composer UI**: `RulePreflightResult` (web) gained `reproposalBlocked`; the review step shows a dedicated "Rule already used" card with the backend reason, and the "Submit to devnet" button is disabled when `reproposalBlocked` (in addition to `needsClarification` / non-VALID). `@tyche/web` typecheck clean.

### 2026-06-14 (PRD — Rule Elimination Decision Phase)

- Motivation (user direction): after the 10-rule finalist set is selected there must be a fixed **1-hour decision window** before the active rule is chosen; during it, Game-Token holders cast **paid elimination votes**; a finalist is eliminated when `elimination_votes > approval_votes`; **up to 5** of the 10 may be eliminated; an elimination vote costs **2× the effective vote fee** for the turn.

Kept a legacy v1 branch so frozen artifacts still validate. Added `getRuleAstJsonSchema()` (native `z.toJSONSchema`) and `MAX_AST_DEPTH`/`MAX_REMOVABLE_NUMBERS`. 6/6 tests.

- **P1 — `packages/rule-test-harness`**: `generateAndRunTests` + bounded Monte-Carlo `classifyDifficulty` (seeded PRNG) for arbitrary ASTs (runtime-safety, determinism, serialization stability, difficulty). Policy decision: only `ALWAYS_TRUE` is degenerate/rejected; extremely rare/hard rules (e.g. jackpot "match 4+ of 6/100", which Monte Carlo cannot distinguish from impossible) are allowed but labelled, to honor the user's freedom directive. **This deviates from the literal PRD §6.8 "reject IMPOSSIBLE" and needs user confirmation.** 6/6 tests.
- **P2 — `packages/rule-compiler` + `apps/api/src/llm.ts`**: replaced regex pattern matching with LLM-emitted AST. New `compileRuleToAst` (apps/api) prompts the model to emit a v2 AST (compact grammar + examples; embedding the full JSON schema stalled the 4B model, so it is conveyed compactly and re-validated by Zod). New async `compileRuleArtifact(request, { astProvider })` keeps the existing provider routing / fallback / disagreement / composite-confidence machinery; the offline regex `validateAndPrecompileRule` remains as the deterministic fallback used by tests. Recursive runtime-bounds + complexity check; difficulty wired in (reject ALWAYS_TRUE). Artifact now carries `schemaVersion`, `ruleMode`, `difficultyClass`, `complexityScore`, `constrainedDecodingUsed`, `testHarnessVersion`. 16/16 tests.

Difficulty (incl. ALWAYS_TRUE / IMPOSSIBLE / TOO_EASY) is a label only and never blocks. The harness/compiler were updated accordingly (removed the difficulty gate). This supersedes the earlier "reject ALWAYS_TRUE" stance.

### 2026-06-14 (Model escalation: gemma3:4b → gemma4:latest)

- Test (user request) showed `gemma4:latest` (8B) compiles the cases `gemma3:4b` got wrong — intent 2 "errar mais" (prose no longer flipped; AST ranking max over `difference`) and intent 5 "1 número e 1 dezena" (correct compound `AND`). So those were a MODEL-capability bottleneck, not a harness defect. ("2 ou mais" is ill-formed phrasing both models over-read; mitigated by user rephrasing.)
- Implemented real escalation in `createRulePreflight` (user-chosen): a `dealerPass(model)` helper runs interpret + compile-from-English + guardian groundedness; the fast primary (`LLM_MODEL`) runs first, and ONLY when it yields an invalid AST or a guardian-flagged drift does it re-try with the stronger `LLM_ESCALATION_MODEL` (`gemma4:latest`) before blocking. The escalation attempt is wrapped in try/catch so a slow/unavailable stronger model never breaks the preflight (it keeps the primary result + surfaces a note). New `RulePreflightResult` fields `escalated` + `modelUsed`. Added `LLM_ESCALATION_MODEL` to `docker-compose.yml` (api) + `.env.example`. `@tyche/api` typecheck clean.
- Live behaviour (single local CPU box): escalation triggers correctly (intent 1 hit `grounded=false` → escalation attempted), but running three models at once (gemma3 4B + gemma4 8B + guardian 8B) thrashes memory and the cold-loaded gemma4 escalation **times out** (>200s) — an environment/resource limit, not a code defect (the single-model run already proved gemma4 compiles intents 2/5 correctly). Mitigations: keep models warm (`OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE`), raise `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`, give the host more RAM/VRAM, or use gemma4:latest as primary on constrained hardware.
- Known guarantee gap (now mitigated, see next): guardian groundedness compares the PROSE interpretation to the rule, so it catches interpretation drift (intent 2) but can miss a case where the prose is plausible while the AST is wrong (observed on intent 5 variance: a wrong ranking AST passed `grounded=true`).
- **Follow-ups implemented:** (1) **`keep_alive: "10m"`** on every LLM + guardian request so models stay resident across the sequential preflight steps (reduces cold-reload timeouts). (2) **Proactive complexity routing** in `createRulePreflight`: `isComplexRule(englishText)` sends rules with negation/inverse (`miss/fewer/fewest/the least/wrong`) or compound connectors (`and/or/both/either`) STRAIGHT to the escalation model, instead of waiting for the (prose-only) guardian to catch a wrong AST — this closes the intent-5 gap. "at least N" is intentionally NOT treated as inverse (it is a threshold the fast model handles). Reactive escalation remains as a backup. (3) The escalation attempt is try/caught so a slow/unavailable strong model never breaks the preflight. Routing decisions verified deterministically; `@tyche/api` typecheck clean; container rebuilt.
- **gemma4:e2b escalation test (2026-06-14):** routed correctly (`escalated:true`, `modelUsed:gemma4:e2b`) and did NOT time out (291s in-container), but produced `decision:INVALID` for the compound rule — the 5.1B model is not capable enough (fails like gemma3:4b). Only the 8B `gemma4:latest` produces the correct compound AST, and it times out here. Net: on this box no local model is both capable (8B) and light enough to run inside the guarded multi-model pipeline within timeout. Decision pending from user (gemma4:latest primary ± guardian / more RAM / accept iteration). `.env` `LLM_ESCALATION_MODEL` left at `gemma4:e2b` pending that choice.
- **Hardware blocker (open):** end-to-end verification of the routed strong-model path on this single CPU box fails — the complex rule routes to `gemma4:latest` correctly, but the 8B cold-load under memory pressure (gemma3 4B + gemma4 8B + guardian 8B competing) exceeds `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS` (180s) → `RULE_AGENT_TIMEOUT`. Correctness of the gemma4 output was already proven in the isolated single-model run; the only failure is load/timing on constrained hardware. Operable options: use a lighter escalation model (`gemma4:e2b`, 5.1B), raise `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`, give the host more RAM, or keep models warm/resident. Also note: the host→container published-port connection resets long preflight requests at ~30s (curl shows `http=000 t=30s`), so the slow guarded path must be exercised in-container or from a client that waits for the first byte.

### 2026-06-14 (Granite Guardian guardrail + English normalization)

- Integrated **IBM Granite Guardian 4.1** (`granite4.1-guardian:8b`, pulled into Ollama) as an independent guardrail in the rule preflight, plus a faithful **translate-to-English** step (cross-language phrasing was a source of ambiguity).
- New `apps/api/src/guardian.ts`: calls the guardian via Ollama's NATIVE `/api/chat` (the `<guardian>` template + `think:false`, parsing `<score>yes|no</score>`). Two checks, calibrated empirically: `detectJailbreak(text)` (jailbreak risk) and `checkGroundedness(rule, interpretation)` (groundedness risk — `yes`=drifted). Feature-flagged by `LLM_GUARDIAN_MODEL`; resolves the native URL from `LLM_BASE_URL` (".../v1" → ".../api/chat").
- New `translateRuleToEnglish` in `apps/api/src/llm.ts`: a faithful translator (preserves polarity/negation/connectors/thresholds) — distinct from the editorializing interpret step.
- `createRulePreflight` flow is now: regex guard → **guardian jailbreak gate** → translate to English → interpret (EN, human message) → **compile AST from the ENGLISH original** (skill) → **guardian groundedness gate**. Submission is blocked if the guardian flags jailbreak or finds the interpretation ungrounded; guardian outages are surfaced (`guardianNote`) and fall back to the regex/compile gates rather than hiding the failure. New `RulePreflightResult` fields: `englishText`, `guardianChecked`, `guardianGrounded`, `guardianNote`. Added `LLM_GUARDIAN_MODEL`/`LLM_GUARDIAN_TIMEOUT_MS` to `docker-compose.yml` (api) and `.env.example`.
- **Live results (gemma3:4b + granite4.1-guardian:8b)**: injection (EN and **PT** "ignore suas instruções…", which the English-only regex misses) → guardian `jailbreak=true` → 400 blocked; "errar mais números" → translated "misses more", AST correct (ranking max over `difference`), but the small interpret model still flipped the PROSE ("lowest missed wins") and the guardian caught it (`grounded=false`) → blocked with "rephrase"; clean rules ("acertar mais", "acertar ≥1") → `grounded=true`, not blocked. So the guardian adds real guarantees (non-English injection coverage + interpretation-drift detection) without false-blocking valid rules.
- Tradeoff recorded: the full guarded preflight now runs up to 5 sequential LLM calls (2 on the 8B guardian), so it is slow (~2–4 min on local CPU). It is feature-flagged — unset `LLM_GUARDIAN_MODEL` to disable. Container `tyche-api` rebuilt and serving the guarded pipeline.
- `@tyche/api` typecheck clean. No milestone checkbox ticked.

### 2026-06-14 (Rule-authoring skill + intent-handling improvements)

- Authored the `compile_rule_to_ast` knowledge as a proper skill (skill-creator format) at `packages/rule-compiler/rule-authoring/`: `SKILL.md` (contract, policy, predicate-vs-ranking decision, node grammar) + `references/patterns.md` (negation/inverse, compound AND/OR, threshold-vs-comparative, "dezena" ambiguity, Portuguese trigger glossary) + `references/examples.md` (worked intent→AST per shape). Validated with `quick_validate.py`.
- `packages/rule-compiler/src/skill.ts` is now a loader that reads the skill folder at runtime and assembles the compile prompt (cached; throws if files are missing — no silent fallback). Bumped `RULE_COMPILER_SKILL_VERSION` to `tyche_rule_compiler_skill_v2` (frozen into the artifact). Dockerfile already `COPY packages` → the markdown ships in the image.
- **Key fix**: `createRulePreflight` now compiles the AST from the ORIGINAL sanitized text (guided by the skill) instead of the prose normalization. A small model can flip polarity while normalizing ("errar mais" → "fewest"); compiling from the original prevents that corrupting the executed rule. The interpret step still produces the human-facing message.
- Hardened the interpret system prompt (`llm.ts`) for polarity/negation, threshold-vs-comparative, compound clauses, and "dezena" ambiguity (human message quality).
- **Intent verification (gemma3:4b, live)** — before → after: "acertar mais" ✓→✓; "errar mais" ✗(invertido)→**✓ corrigido** (ranking max sobre `difference`, P3 com mais erros vence); "acertar ≥1" ✓→✓; "acertar ≥1 dezena" → compila (lê "dezena" como dígito de dezena; ambíguo); "1 número e 1 dezena" → compila VÁLIDO porém AST semanticamente incorreto (não gerou AND) — ainda dependente de iteração/modelo mais forte; "2 ou mais" → ranking (perde o piso ≥2 no fraseado ambíguo). Conclusão: intenções não-ambíguas (contagem/limiar/ranking/negação) agora corretas; intenções genuinamente ambíguas (dezena, composto, "N ou mais") continuam dependentes do modelo — mitigação: iteração do usuário + escalonamento para um provider mais forte (o `astProvider` hoje fixa o gemma3:4b, sem escalonar de fato). O DSL expressa todos os casos (ASTs corretos em `references/examples.md`).
- Verified: `rule-compiler` 17/17 (skill test exercita o loader), `api`/`web`/`worker` typecheck limpos; container `tyche-api` reconstruído e servindo a skill ao vivo (preflight HTTP de "errar mais" → VALID/ranking).

## M3.5 Validation Results

| Requirement                                 | Result                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create verification job per submitted guess | `POST /verification-jobs/create-turn` creates one idempotent job per stored guess receipt for a fulfilled draw.                                   |
| Job payload schema                          | Jobs include `turn_id`, `wallet`, `guess_hash`, `draw_hash`, optional `active_rule_id`, and optional `compiled_artifact_hash`.                    |
| Worker processor                            | `runGuessVerificationCycle` fetches pending jobs, verifies them, completes successful jobs, retries failed jobs, and dead-letters exhausted jobs. |
| Original rule verification                  | Worker evaluates the MVP original rule deterministically as six drawn-number matches.                                                             |
| Alternative rule verification               | Worker evaluates the active rule only when a frozen compiled artifact is present and its hash matches the job payload.                            |
| Runtime-only execution                      | Alternative verification imports `@tyche/rule-runtime` and `@tyche/rule-schema`; it does not call LLMs or the rule compiler.                      |
| Retry policy                                | Failed jobs retry with exponential backoff until `maxAttempts`.                                                                                   |
| Dead-letter queue                           | Exhausted jobs are routed through `deadLetterJob` and counted as `deadLettered`.                                                                  |
| Rate limiting                               | `maxJobsPerCycle` bounds verification/runtime work per cycle.                                                                                     |
| Job status                                  | API tracks `pending`, `processing`, `retry_scheduled`, `completed`, and `dead_letter` statuses.                                                   |
| Result state                                | `POST /verification-results` stores completed results and marks the source job completed.                                                         |
| Backend/admin visibility                    | `GET /verification-jobs`, `GET /verification-results`, and round summaries expose verification state.                                             |

## M4.3 Validation Results

| Requirement                             | Result                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identify creator of active rule         | Creator wallet is read from the active rule proposal selected by the settled election.                                        |
| Check alternative-rule winners          | Reward calculation returns no creator or voter reward when the active alternative rule has zero winners.                      |
| Calculate individual alternative payout | Reward basis uses `WinnerCalculationSummary.alternative.individualPayoutLamports`.                                            |
| Calculate creator reward                | Creator reward is `15%` of the individual alternative payout per alternative winner, subject to cap and reserve availability. |
| Resolve elected-rule voters             | Voters are distinct wallets with recorded votes for the active elected rule.                                                  |
| Calculate voter reward pool             | Voter pool is `15%` of one individual alternative payout, capped and split equally across elected-rule voters.                |
| Fund creator first, then voters         | Creator reward consumes reserve first; voter pool uses only remaining reserve.                                                |
| Do not reduce winner payouts            | Tests verify winner payout remains unchanged while reward records are calculated separately.                                  |
| Store reward records                    | Creator and voter reward records are stored in API projection maps and exposed through summary/endpoints.                     |
| Edge cases                              | Tests cover no alternative winners, multiple alternative winners, and zero elected-rule voters.                               |

### 2026-07-08 (Turn phases: phase-2 pipeline in test mode + 24h production turn)

- Reopened required context before working: `PRD.md`, `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills/tyche-ui-coherence/SKILL.md`, and `.claude/skills/tyche-test-and-verify/SKILL.md`.
- Root cause of "test mode never reaches the shortlist/elimination vote and never draws": `POST /manual/close` (and `/manual/cycle`) shrank the turn to 1 second and called the on-chain `close_turn` directly, so the turn closed before the settlement pipeline could run the finalist shortlist, the elimination decision window, the active-rule election, or the draw; the scheduler then waited forever on `closed_without_fulfilled_draw`.
- Redefined the turn as two sequential phases (PRD §2.1/§5.3/§5.4): phase 1 — create rules + pick numbers, closing at the rule-election/guess cutoff; phase 2 — finalist shortlist, decision/elimination window, active rule, and the draw at the turn's end. Production turns are now fixed 24h = ~22h phase 1 (9167 bps cutoff) + ~2h phase 2, replacing the former `2h → 2h → 8h → 8h` cycle (equal-slot cycle machinery retained).
- Worker: `closeTurnManually` now only ends the phase-1 play window (shrinks the duration to the elapsed time, keeping the turn `Open`) and immediately kicks a settlement pass; the settlement scheduler runs phase 2 end-to-end and issues the real `close_turn`. `/manual/cycle` opens the next turn once settlement has closed the previous one. Added `/manual/force-close` as an explicit escape hatch that keeps the old skip-phase-2 behavior for wedged turns.
- Worker: the settlement view now decodes `start_timestamp` and derives `electionCutoffTimestampSeconds` from the on-chain `rule_election_cutoff_bps` (previously it was hard-set to the turn end), so the finalist shortlist and elimination window run inside phase 2 of the turn and the draw fires at the turn's end.
- Contract source: production defaults updated to `turn_duration_cycle [86400 x4]`, `rule_election_cutoff_bps 9167`, `guess_cutoff_bps 9167`; `validate_config` now accepts equal cutoffs (`<=`), so rule creation and guessing close together at the phase boundary. The deployed devnet program is unchanged and unaffected (the manual-test 2-minute elimination window and existing 7500/9670 cutoffs keep working); the new defaults apply on the next SBF build + deploy + `reinitialize_global_config_for_migration`.
- Web: the home hero timer now shows the current phase with its own countdown — `Phase 1 · Create & play` counts to the cutoff, `Phase 2 · Shortlist & draw` counts to the turn end, and `Draw in progress` covers the settle gap — using the existing pill/ide-num patterns; `phase1EndsAt`/`turnOpen` added to the Tyche context.
- Constants: `TURN_DURATION_CYCLE_HOURS [24 x4]`, `TURN_DURATION_CYCLE_SECONDS [86400 x4]`, new `RULE_ELECTION_CUTOFF_BPS`/`GUESS_CUTOFF_BPS = 9167`; worker `PRODUCTION_TURN_DURATION_CYCLE_SECONDS` matches; `.env`/`.env.example` scale comments updated (56 bps ≈ 8-minute turns on the 24h base).
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @tyche/constants|@tyche/game-engine|@tyche/worker|@tyche/api|@tyche/web typecheck|test|lint|build` all green (worker 86/86, api 63/63, web 16/16); `pnpm --filter @tyche/solana-programs test` (14 core tests, including new equal/zero-cutoff validation asserts) and `lint` (clippy `--all-features`) green in the pinned Docker toolchain.
- Live devnet verification: restarted the native worker with the new code, `POST /manual/cycle` opened turn 93, `POST /manual/close` returned `ended_play_window` (turn kept `Open`), and the settlement pipeline then ran by itself: `project_original_only_election → request_draw → settle_draw (DRAWN) → close_turn → verification/winners/claims → done`; `GET /rounds/93` shows the published draw `[90,34,15,9,54,97]` and the 24h cycle. Turn 93 had no eligible rules, so the shortlist branch was correctly skipped per PRD §6.12; the shortlist/elimination branch itself is covered by the settlement planner unit tests and requires eligible precompiled rules to observe live.

- Root cause: `/round/[turnId]` initializes the single-page shell on the historical Result screen, but `go("home")` and `go("result")` only mutate React state. They do not call the Next.js router, so leaving `/round/24` can render the active round and its latest result while the browser still exposes `/round/24`.
- A browser reload remounts the route from its canonical parameter. `/round/24` therefore restores `initialScreen="result"` and `initialResultTurnId=24`, which correctly reloads result `#0024` according to the stale URL even if the pre-reload client state showed active round `#0030` or another newer round.
- The recent result-selection regression test covers releasing the historical result ID in React state, but it does not assert pathname/history synchronization or reload behavior. This explains why the visible in-session round was corrected while the URL mismatch remained.
- Architecture recommendation: keep `/play` as the stable canonical route for the changing live-round hub and `/round/[turnId]` as an immutable historical permalink whose content always matches its ID. Transitions between them should use real Next.js navigation; internal screen state should remain only for non-resource overlays or steps that do not change the page identity.
- Reviewed the result for inconsistencies: this was a read-only diagnosis of application behavior; no runtime code, route behavior, on-chain state, or milestone status was changed. No milestone checkbox was marked because milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.

### 2026-07-16 (Streamed rule-agent progress and CPU-local model recovery)

- Root cause: the local preflight could perform guardian input screening, translation, primary interpretation, AST compilation, guardian groundedness, and optional stronger-model escalation sequentially. Each model call allowed 300 seconds while the Next.js proxy allowed only 300 seconds for the entire request. Ollama kept `gemma4:latest`, `granite4.1-guardian:8b`, and `gemma4:e2b` resident for 10 minutes, so a CPU-only machine held roughly 25 GB of model data and the proxy returned HTTP 504 before the chain could finish.
- Added real NDJSON progress streaming to the existing `POST /rule-preflight` contract when the client requests `application/x-ndjson`. The API emits bounded high-level stages for input checks, model preparation, safety, optional translation, interpretation, compilation/testing, groundedness, optional escalation, and semantic-impact review. The Next.js Route Handler now forwards the response body without buffering and does not apply its ordinary whole-body timeout after the streamed API has responded; the legacy JSON request/response path remains compatible.
- Replaced the Create chat's three-dot typing bubble with an accessible live activity card using the existing chat surface/tokens. The card has `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, a token-colored spinner, and the current backend-provided action such as `Checking the rule for unsafe instructions...` or `Interpreting your winning condition...`. Pending progress remains available when the user leaves and reattaches to the conversation.
- Reduced the local CPU path without adding a fallback: `gemma4:e2b` escalation is now opt-in and the local `.env`, public example, and Docker default leave it empty; Gemma 4's separate translation pass defaults off; Ollama requests disable reasoning output and bound generated tokens; explicit Ollama tags are no longer incorrectly treated as the same resident model; and AST compilation first uses the model's normalized interpretation so supported normalized rules can use the deterministic compiler instead of another inference call. Thinking control is only sent to detected Ollama endpoints, preserving generic cloud/OpenAI-compatible requests.
- Added regressions for explicit model-tag warmup, Ollama-only reasoning control, streamed stage/result parsing, typed streamed errors, and conversation progress lifecycle. Verified the complete `@tyche/api` ladder (typecheck, tests 87/87, lint with zero warnings, build) and `@tyche/web` ladder (typecheck, tests 79/79, lint with zero warnings, production build). `git diff --check` passed.

### 2026-07-17 (Quick Tunnel PWA hydration recovery)

- Opened the required context before investigating: `PRD.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills`, the Vercel `investigation-mode` skill, the supplied Cloudflare error log, the installed Next.js 16.2.7 `allowedDevOrigins` documentation, the active web configuration, runtime processes, public tunnel endpoints, and the focused PWA browser regression.
- Runtime evidence isolated the failure to the development WebSocket path. The supplied log repeatedly showed `Unable to reach the origin service` with malformed `Unauthorized` responses only for `/_next/webpack-hmr` through `strong-ozone-smallest-knowledgestorm.trycloudflare.com`. Web, admin, API, and worker processes were listening on ports 3000–3003; the public `/play`, `/__api/health`, and `/__worker/health` endpoints returned HTTP 200.
- Reproduced the fault before editing by sending the tunnel hostname and origin through a WebSocket upgrade to local Next.js: the response was malformed/unauthorized. Browser reproduction through the public HTTPS URL loaded server-rendered HTML but failed the standalone hydration assertion, explaining why the installed PWA displayed content while all React interactions appeared dead.
- Root cause: Next.js development mode blocks dev-only assets/endpoints from unlisted origins. A Cloudflare Quick Tunnel receives a random `*.trycloudflare.com` hostname, but `apps/web/next.config.ts` did not allow that development origin.
- Added top-level `allowedDevOrigins: ["*.trycloudflare.com"]` to the web Next.js configuration with a development-tunnel explanation. This is a Next dev-origin permission and does not broaden application CORS or production build origins. Next detected the config change and restarted only the web server automatically.
- Post-fix evidence: the identical WebSocket upgrade now returns `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols` and Next's HMR sync payload instead of `Unauthorized`; the public `/play`, API health, and worker health endpoints remain HTTP 200. The focused Playwright regression against the real public HTTPS tunnel passed 1/1, including standalone hydration, removal of simulated device chrome, and a real React interaction that opens the `Connect your wallet` overlay.
- Verified the complete `@tyche/web` ladder after the fix: typecheck, tests (81/81), lint with zero warnings, and production build all passed. A temporary diagnostic browser helper was removed after use.
- Reviewed for inconsistencies: the fix is limited to development Quick Tunnel access; the production PWA and application API security boundaries were not weakened; persistent WebSocket timeouts were correctly distinguished from failures after the `101` upgrade; no running API/worker process was changed; and no milestone checkbox was marked because milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.

### 2026-07-17 (Installed-PWA MWA permission root-cause diagnosis)

- Reopened the required `PRD.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `PROGRESS_TRACKER.md`, `.claude/skills`, the local `solana-dev` Wallet Standard guidance, and the applicable local MWA setup/connection references. Inspected the active connect call, wallet error presentation, installed `@solana-mobile/wallet-standard-mobile` 0.5.2 flow, transitive MWA protocol implementation, PWA registrar, and service worker.
- User evidence narrowed the failure to the first-time Chrome Local Network Access transition: tapping `Mobile Wallet Adapter` and then `Continue to Allow` produced no native permission prompt and never reached the package's subsequent `Ready to connect!` / `Connect Wallet` action.
- Confirmed the project-side cause: the MWA package deliberately issues `fetch("http://localhost")` from the document to trigger Chrome's loopback/local-network permission, while `apps/web/public/sw.js` intercepts every GET and answers it through `event.respondWith(fetch(event.request))`, including cross-origin loopback requests. Current Chrome documentation states that a service worker cannot trigger the initial Local Network Access prompt; its origin must already have the permission, and the application document must initiate a separate request to obtain it.
- The scoped fix is to leave cross-origin requests, including `http://localhost`, outside the service worker fetch handler while retaining same-origin PWA handling. This allows the MWA document request to remain the permission initiator and preserves the installed PWA surface.
- Reviewed for inconsistencies: no product implementation was changed during this diagnostic request, no wallet authorization was attempted, the service-worker interception was distinguished from Solflare compatibility, and no milestone checkbox was marked because milestone marking requires explicit user confirmation.

- Phase 1 is a token and shared-class change only; no screen markup was restyled yet. Fonts moved from Outfit/Space Grotesk/Sora to **Bevan** (display), **Oswald** (labels), **DM Mono** (numerics) and **Archivo** (body) in `app/layout.tsx`, with `themeColor`, `globals.css` `:root` and `manifest.webmanifest` moved to the `#170B22` ground.
- `features/tyche/tyche.css`: remapped the `.ide-app` variable **values** while keeping every variable **name**, so the screens follow without markup rewrites (`--bg #170B22`, `--surface-2 #0F0618`, `--text #F1E8D6`, `--purple` becomes the brand magenta `#FF2E88`, `--green #7CF6B8`, `--red #FF3B2F`, `--bronze #FF9B4A`, `--num-font 'DM Mono'`). Added the 3a tokens (plate, solid offsets, halos, inset rings, ghost, halftone, dashed, radius scale) and retired `--grad`/`--grad-btn` - 3a has no colour gradient.
- Reshaped the shared classes to the square/solid-offset language: `.ide-card`, `.ide-btn`, `.ide-btn-ghost`, `.ide-pill`, `.ide-chip`, `.ide-stat`, `.ide-seg`, `.ide-tabs`, `.ide-listrow`, `.ide-rulerow`, `.ide-rule-group`, `.ide-numgrid`/`.ide-numcell`, `.ide-result-number*`, `.ide-result-legend`, `.ide-votebtn`, `.ide-balance`, `.ide-bubble-*`, `.ide-nav*`, `.ide-eyebrow`, `.ide-hero-stats`, the phone-shell chrome and the whole Rewards block. `.ide-ambient` became the magenta halftone overlay and `.ide-grad-text` became the offset plate. Added `.ide-plate`, `.ide-live`, `.ide-dashed`, `.ide-diamond`, `.ide-tag` and `.ide-sunburst` for the patterns that repeat across screens.
- `shared.tsx`: `Medal` is now a square Bevan rank plate (gold / bone outline / bronze), `SectionLabel` reuses `.ide-eyebrow`, `ScreenHead` uses the 38 px square back button and a Bevan plate title, `RuleDetail` is a square sheet with a solid orange top edge, and `Confetti` uses the 3a palette. `VoteTally` keeps its SVG arrows rather than switching to the prototype's Unicode glyphs, so its accessible text content - which the e2e suite matches on - is unchanged.
- Two defects found and fixed during the work: replacing `.ide-grad-text` had removed `@keyframes ide-shimmer` while the Rewards loading skeleton still referenced it (the skeleton now uses `rb-pulse`, which is also what `screens.md` specifies), and `.ide-noglow` only matched the inline `ide-pulse` style so it would have stopped covering the new class-based live-badge pulse.
- One deliberate test change, made in the same commit as the CSS: `pwa-display-mode.spec.ts` asserted `.ide-scroll` `padding-top: 52px`; the 3a anatomy specifies 58-62, both values come from `--ide-shell-content-top`, so the assertion moved to `58px`. The standalone `16px` assertion is unchanged because the OS supplies its own inset. The assertion was updated, not loosened.
- Conflict handling: the app's live data always wins over the prototype's mock numbers (invite rewards still derive from `REFERRAL_INVITER_REWARD_ATOMS` and friends, as `Invite.test.ts` asserts), and the app's labels and destinations win over the prototype's (the centre nav slot stays "My rules" rather than the prototype's unlabelled `+` to Play).
- Correction to this entry, made while restyling `Play.tsx` in phase 2: the prototype's "Choose for me" auto-pick was first recorded here as prototype-only functionality with no counterpart in the app. That was wrong. `Play.tsx` already implements it as `quickPick`, labelled "Lucky pick (choose for me)". It is a label difference, not a missing feature, so the app's label was kept and only the control's styling moved to the prototype's cyan ghost pill. Nothing was built to close a gap that did not exist.
- Verification: ESLint with zero warnings, TypeScript typecheck, `250/250` web tests and the webpack production build all pass. Playwright re-run shows **no regressions** - all `11` baseline-passing specs still pass and `17` now pass, the six additional ones being cold-start timeouts in the baseline; among them are the two "no horizontal overflow" specs. Grep gates are clean: zero `var(--grad`, `ide-shimmer`, `Space Grotesk`, `Outfit` and `Sora` references left in `apps/web/src`. Visual sweep at 360/390/430 px across Round, Rules, My rules, Rewards and Account found no horizontal overflow inside `.ide-scroll`, no clipped copy and no page errors; `my-rules.spec.ts` passing confirms taps still reach the UI through the full-screen halftone overlay. Screenshots in the session scratchpad (`shots/`, `gallery/`).
- No milestone checkbox was changed. Phase 2 (per-screen signature work: sunburst hero, skewed live badge, number-chip states, per-screen headings) is not started.

### 2026-08-15 (Retro-cyberpunk rebrand "3a - Tinta Neon", phase 2: screens)

- Opened `PRD.md` (4.1-4.10), `AGENTS.md`, the skills directory, `tyche-design-system` with `references/{components.md,screens.md,screens-html/,screenshots/}` and this tracker before editing. Each screen was compared against its `references/screens-html/NN-*.html` and `references/screenshots/NN-*.png`.
- `Home.tsx` (01): Bevan plate wordmark; `Connect` as the small yellow pill with the magenta halo; the phase-1 live state now uses the skewed red badge with the pulsing square, while every other phase stays a neutral status chip; masked twin conic prize rays plus the magenta/cyan halo, both `pointer-events: none` and behind the content; prize split into Bevan 70 px with the plate, gold decimals and a DM Mono cyan unit; dashed rule with the gold diamond; the counters became the two square stat blocks; "Create your rule" became the highlighted card with the cyan `with AI` tag, a DM Mono input and the 46 px arrow button; "The rules" became a plate title with a rule and a DM Mono `vote` exit; rule rows carry Oswald uppercase titles and a magenta ring on the leader.
- `Play.tsx` (02-04): Oswald `clear` label, Oswald instruction, DM Mono `n/6 selected` in yellow, the auto-pick control restyled to the cyan ghost pill, square empty slots with an inset ring, and the terminal state's heading as a large plate. The disabled CTA keeps naming what is missing ("6 numbers left").
- `Vote.tsx` (05-06): plate screen title, the gate as a highlighted card with a solid orange offset and a Bevan heading, Oswald uppercase rule titles, and finalist cards whose state is carried by the inset ring - cyan when safe, yellow when at risk, red with `opacity: .65` when eliminated.
- `Create.tsx` (07): the interpretation title moved to Bevan uppercase and its normalized text to DM Mono, matching the prototype's pseudocode treatment.
- `Result.tsx` and `DrawResult.tsx` (08-09): Bevan plate headings, `You won!` as the Oswald `.3em` eyebrow with a Bevan plate amount and DM Mono cyan unit, the elected rule in Bevan yellow, the modal as a square block with a solid orange offset, the settled marker as the skewed red badge, drawn numbers as bone chips with a magenta offset, and a square close button.
- Screens not individually restyled (`Rewards`, `Profile`, `Claims`, `Guesses`, `MyRules`, `Invite`, `Share`, `Connect`) already inherit the language from phase 1: `ScreenHead` gives them Bevan plate titles, and their cards, pills, tabs, inputs, rows and buttons come from the reshaped `.ide-*` classes. They were reviewed in the gallery and are coherent; deeper per-screen detail remains available if wanted.
- Conflict log for this phase. Case A (kept and restyled): every state the prototype never draws - loading, error, empty, pending-in-wallet, the elimination window, and the full Rewards treasury/epoch/lock surface. Case B (visual only): the prize rays, halftone, skewed badge, dashed diamond and plate were adopted; no prototype-only functionality was built. Case C (app data wins): every figure stays bound to its live source - pool, turn id, player and rule counts, entry and vote fees, and the invite constants. Case D (app structure wins, listed for your decision): the centre nav slot keeps "My rules" instead of the prototype's unlabelled `+` to Play; the rules list keeps the grouped card introduced on 2026-08-10 rather than the prototype's separate per-row blocks; `PLAY NOW` keeps its bolt icon and live fee suffix; and `VoteTally` keeps SVG arrows instead of the prototype's Unicode triangles so its accessible text is unchanged.
- Verification: ESLint with zero warnings, TypeScript typecheck and `250/250` web tests pass. Playwright shows **no regressions** - `17` passing, the identical set to phase 1 and a superset of the recorded baseline, with zero specs lost against either. The first phase-2 Playwright run reported `0` passing; that was an environment fault, not a regression - a mock dev server was still holding port 3000 and Next 16 permits only one dev server per app dir, so the test server could not start. It was stopped and the run repeated cleanly. Gallery sweep across all ten mock screens reports no horizontal overflow inside any phone shell and no page errors.
- No milestone checkbox was changed. Final consistency review confirms tokens-only styling, English UI copy, unchanged data bindings and unchanged voting, fee and submission behaviour.
